# jj-store

This reference describes the application command parser. See [capabilities](../reference/capabilities.md) for profile and qualification limits.

### Native JJ server

Run a persistent LocalTrusted native repository service with the embedded RustFS
runtime. Start with `jj-store init --local --state-dir PATH`, then pass the
generated `PATH/server.toml` to `jj-store run`. The process stays in the
foreground and owns both the loopback browser/RPC listeners and RustFS child. No
user credential or separately installed storage service is required.

Use `jj-store help -k commands` for the command guide. Repository creation and
native client operations use the custom `jj store` command family.

An optional `web_root` configuration field serves a prebuilt browser bundle from
the same origin. It is resolved relative to the configuration file. See
[Repository browser](../guides/browsing.md) for build and acceptance instructions.
Startup rejects missing, oversized or unsafe listed assets. Authenticated shared
serving and external object storage are deferred beyond the local release.

Local stack workspaces also run directly through `jj-store stack`, without a
server or registration. Start with
`jj-store stack init --name NAME --target BOOKMARK` in an ordinary Git-backed JJ
workspace; use `jj-store help stack` for workspace, branch, content, conflict
and native history commands.


```text
Usage: jj-store [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]
```

| Argument or option | Meaning | Default / values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | Output presentation. JSON retains full identities, versions and response variants for automation. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: text; Values: text, json |
| `--no-pager <NO_PAGER>` | Write output directly instead of invoking the configured pager. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--color <COLOR>` | Control terminal color rendering independently of the output data format. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: auto; Values: auto, always, never |
| `-h, --help` | Print help (see a summary with '-h') |  |

## jj-store token

Administer repository-scoped tokens through the authenticated native API.

```sh
jj-store token generate
jj store token list --endpoint https://store.example --repo-id REPOSITORY_ID
jj-store token list --endpoint https://store.example --repo-id REPOSITORY_ID
```

Both command families use the same repository admin credential from the OS
facility or `JJ_STORE_TOKEN`. An operator credential grants no repository
access. Connection flags belong to `list`, `grant`, `revoke`, `status`, and
`retry`; `--format json` returns structured results without a pager.

`generate` creates one manual bearer credential locally, prints it once and does
not store it. Grant that same credential independently to each repository that
it should discover. Repository policies retain separate permissions, expiry and
revocation, so removing it from one repository does not affect the others.

`grant --principal ID --permission read|write|admin --request PATH` adds a
client-generated token. Supply its complete bearer credential through a hidden
prompt, `--token-stdin`, or `JJ_STORE_GRANT_TOKEN`. The grant credential is
separate from the admin credential. Optional `--expires-at UNIX_SECONDS` sets
its expiry. No secret is accepted in arguments, printed, or saved in the
journal.

`revoke --token-id ID --request PATH` removes a grant. Both mutations retain the
exact snapshot, principal, request ID and intent in a bounded local request file
outside checkouts before publication. Existing request files must match the
original intent; a stale request never silently refreshes its snapshot.

`status --request PATH` checks the durable receipt without publishing. An
`unknown` result means no receipt was observed; it does not prove rejection.
`retry --request PATH` reapplies the exact saved request. Grant status/retry
needs the original grant credential through the same hidden/stdin/environment
input; revoke requires none. Keep that credential in its OS facility or secret
manager. Current admin authorization and the original principal are required for
every receipt read. Rotation to another admin token for the same principal is
allowed.

Keep request records for recovery. If a request is stale, inspect current token
state before deliberately creating a new request file. Never overwrite or delete
a journal to make an uncertain publication look like a new operation.


```text
Usage: jj-store token [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>
```

| Argument or option | Meaning | Default / values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | Output presentation. JSON retains full identities, versions and response variants for automation. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: text; Values: text, json |
| `--no-pager <NO_PAGER>` | Write output directly instead of invoking the configured pager. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--color <COLOR>` | Control terminal color rendering independently of the output data format. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: auto; Values: auto, always, never |
| `-h, --help` | Print help (see a summary with '-h') |  |

outside checkouts before publication. Existing request files must match the
original intent; a stale request never silently refreshes its snapshot.

`status --request PATH` checks the durable receipt without publishing. An
`unknown` result means no receipt was observed; it does not prove rejection.
`retry --request PATH` reapplies the exact saved request. Grant status/retry
needs the original grant credential through the same hidden/stdin/environment
input; revoke requires none. Keep that credential in its OS facility or secret
manager. Current admin authorization and the original principal are required for
every receipt read. Rotation to another admin token for the same principal is
allowed.

Keep request records for recovery. If a request is stale, inspect current token
state before deliberately creating a new request file. Never overwrite or delete
a journal to make an uncertain publication look like a new operation.

## jj-store run

### Run the foreground server

Start with `jj-store run --config PATH`. The listening event identifies the
bound address; storage readiness is checked separately with `doctor` against a
known repository. `--format json` emits a plain JSON event without a pager.

Ctrl-C and termination request graceful shutdown. After five seconds a stuck
request is canceled; clients must treat interrupted publications as unknown
outcomes and retry with their original identities. A second process using the
same state directory fails explicitly. Stop the old process before restarting.

Desktop hosts can opt into `--desktop-supervised` with a pipe on stdin. EOF
requests graceful shutdown. This mode requires strict LocalTrusted embedded
storage and accepts launch-only `--desktop-bind`, `--desktop-web-root` and
`--desktop-rustfs-executable` overrides. It leaves stored configuration
unchanged. Overrides require supervision; an ordinary terminal is not an owner
pipe.


```text
Usage: jj-store run [OPTIONS] --config <CONFIG>
```

| Argument or option | Meaning | Default / values |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--config <CONFIG>` | Path to the strict server TOML configuration for this operation. Required. |  |
| `--loopback-only <LOOPBACK_ONLY>` | Require a literal loopback bind address | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--desktop-supervised <DESKTOP_SUPERVISED>` | Stop the local service when its desktop owner's stdin pipe closes | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--desktop-bind <DESKTOP_BIND>` | Override the literal-loopback listener for this supervised launch only |  |
| `--desktop-web-root <DESKTOP_WEB_ROOT>` | Use the current app bundle's production browser assets |  |
| `--desktop-rustfs-executable <DESKTOP_RUSTFS_EXECUTABLE>` | Use the current app bundle's paired RustFS executable |  |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | Output presentation. JSON retains full identities, versions and response variants for automation. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: text; Values: text, json |
| `--no-pager <NO_PAGER>` | Write output directly instead of invoking the configured pager. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: false; Values: true, false |
| `--color <COLOR>` | Control terminal color rendering independently of the output data format. Inherited by subcommands. | Default: auto; Values: auto, always, never |
| `-h, --help` | Print help (see a summary with '-h') |  |

## jj-store config

### Server configuration

Use `init --local --state-dir PATH` to generate the supported strict format-2
configuration, and `config check --config PATH/server.toml` to validate it.
Older formats are rejected; this unreleased application has no compatibility or
migration command. Paths are relative to the configuration file. Keep state
outside Git/JJ checkouts. Unknown keys and invalid budgets fail.
`config example` documents authenticated access with external S3 authority.
Initialize its private installation identity and empty repository catalog with
`jj-store registry init --state-dir PATH`, then reference those two files from
`[access]`. External-provider release qualification remains deferred; this is
not the LocalTrusted application setup path.

Format 2 tags `[access]` and `[storage]`, and accepts repeated `[[backup]]`
targets. Run `init --local --state-dir PATH` for the supported application
deployment: a LocalTrusted installation with managed RustFS, private internal
identity and credentials, an empty local repository catalog, an explicit
persistent volume, and backups disabled.

Format 2 names environment or OS-credential references explicitly. Secret values
are never accepted in TOML. A new managed installation creates its bucket once,
publishes and verifies the installation sentinel, then requires both on every
restart. Manual-token authenticated repository discovery is implemented. Shared
deployment release qualification, external S3 provider qualification, backup
targets and restore remain future work.

Shared listeners require TLS certificate and private-key paths. Plain HTTP is
allowed only for an explicitly enabled literal loopback listener and endpoint.
The default request limits are eight concurrent requests, 30 seconds and 32 MiB
per native blob. Configure one serving instance per storage namespace; the local
state lock does not provide distributed fencing.

Native background search indexing is opt-in: add one `[[search]]` entry per
repository with `repository` and `token_environment`, whose name starts with
`JJ_STORE_SEARCH_TOKEN_` for authenticated access. Supply a read token for that
repository in the named environment variable. LocalTrusted indexing uses the
installation principal and does not require that token reference. Use the
existing token administration commands to issue/revoke it; the server never
creates search credentials or reads them from a checkout. Rotate by restarting
with the replacement environment value.

`search.source.scopes.<scope>` selects `kind = "bookmark"` or `"workspace"` and
a native name. With no scopes, only retained metadata is indexed. Source options
include `index_source`, `include_prefixes`, `exclude_prefixes`,
`max_text_bytes`, `max_files`, `max_work` and `max_output_bytes`. Paths are
native prefixes; exclusions affect only the derived index. Changed source
configuration rebuilds the index at restart before serving it.

Per-entry defaults are `poll_millis = 1000`, `timeout_seconds = 60`,
`index_bytes = 536870912` per generation and `snapshot_every = 32` committed
source positions. Set `snapshot_every = 0` to disable optional immutable remote
index snapshots. At most eight repositories may be configured. Each runner uses
one native extraction worker and a 32 MiB Tantivy writer, retains at most 16
generations, and admits at most 100,000 documents. Each batch caps 100,000
requests, 256 MiB transferred and 16 MiB per object; server inventory limits
also apply. Pinned pages can retain old generations, so provision disk for
retained generations plus a staging generation.

Indexes live under `state_dir/search/<repository>`, with private directory
permissions; writer leases live under `state_dir/adapters`. The running server
owns and cancels these workers. Search faults degrade indexing independently of
native repository serving. `/v1/repos/{repository}/search/status` reports live
freshness; `jj-store doctor` reads that endpoint with the caller's token.

### Writable replication

Add one `[[replication]]` entry for each local repository that should exchange
accepted publications with one independently writable upstream:

```toml
[[replication]]
repository = "00000000000000000000000000000000"
upstream = "https://jj.example.test/"
token_environment = "JJ_STORE_REPLICATION_TOKEN_MAIN"
ca_certificate = "./upstream-ca.pem"
```

Issue a write token for the same repository on the upstream and place it only in
the named environment variable before starting `jj-store`. Names must begin with
`JJ_STORE_REPLICATION_TOKEN_`. The configuration stores the name, never the
credential. The server resolves the credential lazily into memory and
re-resolves it after a transport failure, which allows token rotation without
putting credentials in a checkout or status response.

Upstreams require HTTPS. A literal loopback HTTP endpoint additionally requires
`insecure_loopback = true`. At most eight repositories may be configured and a
repository may appear only once. Each entry can override the bounded defaults
under `[replication.limits]`: 128 origins per page, 100,000 closure entries,
100,000 objects and 1 GiB per step, 64 MiB per native object, a five-second
poll, 500 ms initial retry, 60-second maximum retry, an eight-failure circuit,
60-second circuit cooldown and a 30-second control timeout.

The server starts and stops every configured worker with its own lifecycle.
Remote failure degrades replication only; foreground repository reads and
mutations remain local. Durable push and pull checkpoints live in the local
authoritative object store. Accepted imports wake committed-change SSE and, when
search is configured for that repository, advance the search adapter from the
destination WAL position.

The initial activation profile is qualified by focused configuration, lifecycle,
outage, authenticated RPC, worker, SSE and search-projection tests. Exhaustive
pressure and fault soak, expanded memory and disk matrices, browser replication
UI, cold two-instance real-RustFS replication, pressure archive or export
tooling and additional deployment topologies are deferred.

## jj-store doctor

### Diagnose an existing repository

`jj-store doctor --config PATH --repo-id ID` checks repository authorization and
selected operation heads through the in-process service and configured RustFS.
It uses `JJ_STORE_TOKEN` or the OS credential for the configuration's public
URL. It publishes no operations and does not reconcile multiple heads.

A successful result establishes access to current authoritative metadata.
Adapters report separately; this is not a full retained-history integrity audit.

For configured search, doctor also queries the running server's authenticated
search status route with the same repository token. It reports ready, stale,
degraded, not-ready, access-denied or unavailable search independently of
`storage_ready`. The structured result includes live durable/served positions
when available. Requests have a five-second cap, do not follow redirects and
bound response bytes. A stopped listener therefore leaves search unavailable;
doctor does not open the index or start an indexer. TLS uses normal verification
plus the configured server certificate as a trust root.

## jj-store operator

### Operator credentials

The local operator policy authorizes repository creation or installation
identity management through separate capabilities.
`--permission manage-identities` selects identity management; the default is
`create-repository`. It never grants access to repository contents.
`operator init` creates a policy; an identical retry is safe. `operator grant`
adds an explicitly selected credential. `operator list` shows public grant
metadata, and `operator revoke` removes one token ID.

Provision with a canonical `--endpoint`, an explicit `--principal` identity, and
`--policy PATH` outside checkouts. `JJ_STORE_OPERATOR_TOKEN` supplies an
existing automation credential. Otherwise provisioning reuses or creates a token
in the OS credential facility for that endpoint. Secrets never appear in output.
Policy files retain only verifiers and are reloaded for each creation request.

Repository credentials remain separate: `JJ_STORE_TOKEN` or `jj store login`. No
plaintext credential fallback is available.

Use `jj-store token` for repository grants and revocations. Those requests
require a current repository admin credential; the creation operator cannot
authorize them.

Use `jj-store token generate` once when one manual credential should access
several repositories. Grant it separately through each repository policy; the
installation registry uses its public token ID only to find candidates and each
repository reauthorizes the complete credential.

Use `jj-store identity --endpoint ENDPOINT` to list, grant or revoke
installation identity bindings. A grant binds an existing user token to a
profile principal; repository grants remain independent. Supply the user token
on stdin with `grant --principal ID --token-stdin --request PATH`. The operator
credential comes from the platform facility or `JJ_STORE_OPERATOR_TOKEN`.
Mutation journals stay outside checkouts, contain only public intent, and retain
the original request ID. `status --request PATH` and a retry with the same
journal recover uncertain outcomes. Revoked token IDs cannot be reassigned to
another principal.
